details: On June 22, 2026, the U.S. Senate passed the "21st Century Housing Road Act" with an overwhelming vote of 85-5. A key additional clause in the bill prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (CBDC) or any substantially similar digital assets before the end of 2030, even if issued indirectly through financial institutions. The bill explicitly exempts private stablecoins, such as USDC and USDT, effectively preserving their market position and favoring private digital dollar innovation over a state-issued alternative. This legislative action reflects growing opposition to a U.S. CBDC among policymakers, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh having previously expressed concerns about its privacy implications and policy choices.
title: US Senate Bans Federal Reserve CBDC Until 2030, Boosts Stablecoins

details: China's Ministry of Commerce announced on June 22, 2026, new trade restrictions targeting 10 American companies. These firms, involved in defense, aerospace, and rare earth mining, are now banned from exporting dual-use goods (items with both civilian and military applications) from China. This action is a direct retaliation to Washington's recent expansion of its military-linked blacklist of Chinese companies, including major tech giants. The measures escalate the ongoing tit-for-tat economic confrontation between the two global superpowers, impacting critical supply chains for rare earth materials used in defense systems, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics, where China holds significant global influence.
title: China Sanctions US Firms in Escalating Trade War Over Rare Earths & Tech

details: On June 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated three individuals and six entities for facilitating financial transactions on behalf of the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) using cryptocurrencies. The enforcement action targets a Syria-based money services business called Bitcoin Xchange, which has reportedly transferred funds for ISIS associates from multiple countries, including the United States. OFAC also identified two TRON wallet addresses linked to a designated ISIS financial facilitator. This highlights the ongoing challenge of illicit finance within the crypto ecosystem and underscores the importance for global virtual asset service providers (VASPs) and financial institutions to update their sanctions screening and transaction monitoring protocols.
title: US Sanctions ISIS Crypto Facilitators, Highlighting Illicit Use

details: On June 22, 2026, the European Union introduced its 20th package of sanctions against Russia, targeting its energy revenues, military-industrial complex, financial services, and trade. This package includes a new legal mechanism empowering EU Member State courts to order Russian parties to cease retaliatory proceedings brought in Russia in breach of arbitration agreements, with potential financial penalties for non-compliance. These sanctions are part of the EU's ongoing response to Russia's war in Ukraine and aim to limit Russia's economic capacity, with broader implications for international trade and financial relations.
title: EU Imposes 20th Sanctions Package on Russia, Targets Financial Services
